sections.title: AI Agent Applications for Seattle Organizations
sections.description: Production AI agent solutions for Seattle's leading organizations.

blocks.heading: Amazon Ecosystem Agents
paragraphs: For Amazon's vast seller community and the technology companies building on AWS:

Amazon Seller Central agents: Autonomous agents managing product listing optimization, inventory replenishment signals, pricing strategy responses, and review management for Amazon sellers operating in Seattle's massive FBA community — reducing the manual operational burden of large-scale Amazon marketplace operations.

AWS infrastructure agents: Autonomous DevOps agents for AWS-native organizations — monitoring costs, suggesting resource optimization, identifying security vulnerabilities, and generating infrastructure-as-code updates for Seattle's deeply AWS-standardized technology companies.

eCommerce operations agents: Multi-step workflow agents handling customer service escalations, return merchandise authorization, supplier communication, and inventory exception resolution for Seattle's eCommerce companies.
Cost: $55,000–$145,000 | Timeline: 12–22 weeks | AWS-native

blocks.heading: Aerospace and Supply Chain Agents
paragraphs: For Boeing (Seattle/Everett) and Seattle's aerospace supply chain:

RFQ and procurement agents: Agents processing incoming RFQ requests, gathering supplier qualifications, collecting bids, comparing responses, and routing recommendation packages to procurement managers — reducing the manual effort of Boeing's complex supplier management.

Engineering documentation agents: Agents monitoring for engineering change order notifications, extracting material impacts, cross-referencing against current production orders, and flagging affected components for engineering review.
Supplier performance monitoring: Autonomous agents tracking delivery performance, quality metrics, and financial health signals for Boeing's multi-tier supply chain.
Cost: $60,000–$155,000 | Timeline: 12–24 weeks

blocks.heading: Healthcare Coordination Agents
paragraphs: For UW Medicine, Providence Health, and Swedish Health:

Care coordination agents: Post-discharge follow-up agents contacting high-risk patients, monitoring care plan adherence, scheduling follow-up appointments, and escalating concerning responses to clinical staff for Seattle's health systems' chronic disease management programs.

Prior authorization agents: Automated PA submission for Washington state's major payers (Premera, Regence/Cambia, Molina) with status monitoring and appeal initiation for Seattle's health systems' high-volume PA workload.

Clinical research coordination agents: Autonomous agents managing research participant communication, visit scheduling, and data collection workflows for UW Medicine's substantial clinical research programs.
Cost: $55,000–$150,000 | Timeline: 12–24 weeks | HIPAA BAA

blocks.heading: Research and Competitive Intelligence Agents
paragraphs: For Microsoft, Amazon, Zillow, Expedia, and Seattle's large technology employer community:

Competitive intelligence agents: Autonomous agents monitoring competitor product updates, pricing changes, job postings (indicating R&D direction), patent filings, and press releases — synthesizing daily competitive intelligence briefings for Seattle technology product teams.
Technical research agents: Agents searching arXiv, GitHub, and technical publications for relevant AI and technology research — surfacing new techniques relevant to Seattle engineering teams' work.
Market research agents: Autonomous market research assembling consumer sentiment, industry data, and competitive landscape for Seattle's product and strategy teams.
Cost: $50,000–$130,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks

sections.title: Building Agents for Amazon's Operational Excellence Standard
sections.description: Amazon's 'working backwards' product philosophy and operational excellence culture create specific agent quality expectations.

blocks.heading: Deterministic where possible
paragraphs: Seattle engineering culture prefers agents with predictable, auditable behavior over agents with emergent behavior. ClickMasters designs Seattle agents with maximum determinism — using structured outputs, function calling (not free-text tool invocation), and explicit branching logic rather than relying on model reasoning for consequential decisions.

blocks.heading: Runbooks before agents
paragraphs: For each Seattle agent, ClickMasters provides a 'runbook' — a human-readable document describing exactly what the agent does, what tools it uses, what decisions it makes, and what it escalates to humans. This runbook-first approach ensures Seattle operations teams can manage, debug, and own agents after deployment.

blocks.heading: Cost optimization by design
paragraphs: Amazon's culture of infrastructure cost management extends to AI agents. ClickMasters designs Seattle agents with token efficiency, result caching, and model selection (using smaller models for classification steps, larger models only for complex reasoning) that keeps operating cost proportional to business value.
